segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I own air permit compliance for the whole site... figure out what actually happened, decide what needed to be reported to the state, and keep production moving if I could justify it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant states role responsibilities and operational objectives without a manifested hidden bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My first read was that it was probably drift again... once I had that in my head... I read them as consistent with drift rather than as a red flag on their own.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The early drift hypothesis is explicitly described as shaping interpretation of later ambiguous handheld readings, matching the Primacy Effect instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The readings he brought back were elevated, but not dramatically... We were also mid-batch on a large customer order due in two days, so a shutdown wasn't something anyone wanted to trigger without good reason.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This expresses ambiguous evidence and legitimate production constraints, but does not by itself establish a hidden bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I decided to hold off on pulling the full continuous emissions monitoring data... If it had come back showing an exceedance, we'd have been on a 24-hour reporting clock... So I told myself the grey-zone readings weren't conclusive enough.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant acknowledges the more diagnostic step and links deferral partly to the unwelcome reporting consequence, matching the Ostrich effect instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Gasket seep... is genuinely our most common issue... But the Ohio valve failure was just very present for me... the valve scenario is what I wrote down and what I asked maintenance to check first.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A vivid recent valve-failure narrative displaced the statistically common gasket explanation in the initial causal framing, matching Imaginability Bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once the gasket was confirmed, I had two methodologies I could reasonably apply... picked the one I felt was most defensible given how our last few audits went.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The generation specification deliberately leaves decision point 4 as an undetermined judgment call without intended bias instrumentation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Early on, fairly confident it was drift—maybe too confident... If the field readings that first morning had been sharper... that would have changed how much weight I put on the drift explanation.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is retrospective confidence calibration and a counterfactual about evidence sharpness; it does not introduce a separate hidden instance.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the run detects 2 of 3 positive segments with no false alarms (hit rate 0.6667; F1 0.8000).
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Strict instance identification is 0/3 at every threshold because both identified labels are near neighbors and the Ostrich-effect match remains candidate-only.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first identification reaches 2/3 at the recommended threshold (F1 0.8000) and 3/3 when candidates are included, with two candidate-related instance false positives.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Candidates add one useful mechanism-level recovery for the Ostrich-effect instance, but also add one unsupported negative-segment alarm and one duplicate claim.
main_failure_modes: No hidden target label is matched strictly.
The Primacy Effect and Imaginability Bias mechanisms are reported under near-neighbor labels.
The Ostrich-effect mechanism is withheld as a candidate rather than identified.
The candidate tier introduces overconfidence speculation and a duplicate availability claim.
main_strengths: Evidence quotations are valid and well localized.
The two identified findings and the useful candidate capture the intended mechanisms with full overlap.
The output explicitly discloses absent retrieval support and mixed operational explanations.
The RAG correctly avoids asserting a separate overconfidence finding as identified.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This is a taxonomy-sensitive run: mechanism recognition is substantially stronger than strict label recognition. At the recommended threshold, it is a strong mechanism-level detector with no segment false alarms, but it would score poorly under a strict closed-label evaluation.
